Import as `./support/harness.mjs`. Do NOT edit server.mjs or the harness. Use one server per describe block (fresh temp DATA_FILE) where state matters; assert in each error case that no booking was created when relevant. Helper idea: `expectError(res, status, message)` -> strictEqual status, content-type JSON_TYPE, deepStrictEqual(res.json(), {error: message}). Cases: Routing (send via http.request path or rawRequest — never fetch): - GET /api/rooms -> 200 {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']} exact, JSON content type. `/api/rooms?x=1` also 200. - 404 `not found` for: /api/%62ookings, /api/./rooms (rawRequest — http.request may keep it, but use raw to be sure), /API/rooms, /api/bookings/ , /api/bookings/1/, /api/bookings//1, /api/rooms/, /api, /index.html, /app.js/ , //api/rooms, /api/bookings%2F1 ... careful: `/api/bookings%2F1` is NOT under prefix `/api/bookings/` so 404. Make sure byte counts use Buffer.byteLength and multi-byte chars: a 10001-byte body made of a JSON string with 'é' chars (2 bytes each) whose JS length is < 10000 -> 413. 413 beats 400: 10001 bytes of 'x' -> 413. Also chunked transfer encoding (http.request without Content-Length, writing several chunks totalling 10001 bytes) -> 413. 3. 400 `body must be a JSON object`: '', ' ', 'not json', 'null', '[]', '[{}]', '"s"', '1', 'true', '{', BOM (Buffer [0xEF,0xBB,0xBF] + JSON of B) -> 400 (BOM kept). '{}' -> passes rule 3 and fails rule 4 (room message). 4. room 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`: missing, 'aurora', 'Aurora ', ' Aurora', 1, null, ['Aurora'], 'Dune'. Room checked before title: {..., room:'x', title:''} -> room message. 5. title 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`: missing, '', ' ', 5, null, 81 'a's, ' ' + 81 'a's. Start before end: {start:'x', end:'x'} -> start message. 8. end 400 `end must be HH:MM`: same kinds; end '24:00' with start '23:00' -> end message (not 'after'). OK: start '23:58' end '23:59' -> 201; start '00:00' end '00:01' -> 201. 9. 400 `end must be after start`: end == start ('09:00','09:00'); end < start ('10:00','09:00'). 10. 409 `room is already booked from to `: with Aurora 09:00-10:00 and Aurora 11:00-12:00 on 2026-11-03 existing: new 09:30-11:30 -> `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00` (earliest-starting overlap, even when the later one was created first — create 11:00-12:00 FIRST then 09:00-10:00 to defeat 'first in array' implementations); 10:00-11:00 -> 201 (touching both); 08:00-09:00 -> 201; same times in Borealis -> 201; same times on another date -> 201; 09:59-10:00 -> 409 from 09:00 to 10:00. Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). 4 5 Server 6 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 7 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 20 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 21 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 26 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 27 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 28 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 29 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 30 31 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 32 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 33 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 34 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 35 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 36 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 37 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 38 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 39 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 40 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 41 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 42 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 43 44 Page 45 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 46 - The page loads the script with a `

content.text:
I wrote the tests as two files, since the total came to 652 lines. All 196 tests pass, and I found no suspected server bugs. I didn't change `server.mjs` or the harness.

- **`/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/server-api.test.mjs`** (276 lines) covers routing, 404 and 405 for every listed method including HEAD, query handling, page serving, DELETE, content types, and the ordering, `?date` and 400 cases for `GET /api/bookings`.
- **`/root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/server-rules.test.mjs`** (376 lines) covers booking rules 1-10, the precedence checks between rules, the 201 reply shape and the ids.

I ran `node --test test/server-api.test.mjs test/server-rules.test.mjs`, which ran 196 tests across 15 suites with 0 failures. Each suite starts its own server with a fresh temp `DATA_FILE`. Servers and temp dirs are cleaned up in `after` hooks, and there is no `console.log`.

Two cases differ from your list:

1. **Raw UTF-8 id `٢` in DELETE.** Node's HTTP parser rejects non-ASCII bytes in the request target and answers 400 before `server.mjs` runs, so a strict 404 `booking not found` can't be tested. That one test asserts only that the reply is 400 or 404 and that booking 2 is not deleted. This is a limit of Node's parser, not a server bug.
2. **`?date=2026-11-03&date=`.** I had listed this as a 400 case, but the first `date` value wins, so the server correctly returns 200. I removed it.

`/api/bookings/%2F` has a 405 test for GET, POST, PUT and OPTIONS, plus the 404 `booking not found` test for DELETE, which your list didn't spell out.
